Video-side facts to merge into its +0x14 / +0x18 members: vertexStreams is boost::intrusive_ptr<video::CVertexStreams> (the constructor 0x6b88a8 calls CVertexStreams::allocate on the address of +0x14), and primitiveStream / primitiveWord_1c..primitiveHalf_2e are one embedded video::CPrimitiveStream (+0x18 intrusive_ptr<IBuffer> m_indexBuffer, +0x1c m_offset, +0x20 m_count, +0x24 m_vertexStart, +0x28 m_vertexEnd, +0x2c m_indexType, +0x2e m_primitiveType), copied member by member with a use of the index buffer. glitch-video declares scene::CMeshBuffer in video_types.hpp and uses it by pointer in IVideoDriver::draw (+0x58) and drawMeshBuffer.
action: keep: canonical (u1-scene); adopt the video member types

differences: Stand-in for the two members createTriangles calls: map(std::int32_t access) (non-const) and unmap() (non-const). The canonical IBuffer has map(E_BUFFER_READ_MAP_ACCESS) const at 0x5a1adc (the batch passes the constant 1) and unmap() const at 0x637a68, plus the non-const map(E_BUFFER_MAP_ACCESS) 0x5a19f0; both aliases are int32_t, so a call on a non-const buffer picks the writing overload. createTriangles must call the read mapping through a const reference. The binary decides: the canonical class is right.
action: replace with #include; call map through a const IBuffer&

differences: The stand-in uses a raw IBuffer* buffer and the names valueType (+0x0a), componentCount (+0x0c), stride (+0x0e). The canonical entry holds boost::intrusive_ptr<IBuffer> and names the three words field0a (value type, index into SVertexAttributeTypeInspection::ValueTypeSize), field0c (component count) and field0e (per-vertex stride); offsets and sizes agree (16 bytes). The binary decides: the canonical names are right.
action: replace with #include; rename valueType/componentCount/stride to field0a/field0c/field0e
